statement: Share of firms using AI to produce goods or services >= 2x its 2025 average (Bloc A Census Bureau BTOS; 2027Q4)
status_at_phase_end: Data gap at the timeline start. The designated survey (BTOS) was running biweekly from mid-2022 but did not yet ask about AI use (the AI question was added in September 2023). The most recent official firm-level AI adoption evidence was the 2018 Annual Business Survey technology module, which found advanced-technology adoption including AI to be rare and skewed to large, older firms.

items.summary: Bloc A statistics agency announced a new biweekly business survey (successor to its pandemic small-business pulse survey), with collection from mid-July 2022 covering performance, employment, demand and prices; no AI-use question was part of the announced content.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau, 'BTOS Expands Small Business Pulse Survey, Will Conduct Continuous Data Collection', 2022-06-23 (verified via web_extract this run). The current BTOS data page (also opened) notes the all-employer-business scope from 2023-09-11; the AI supplement began in the 2023 survey cycle, after this window.

items.summary: Bloc A statistics agency's 2018 business survey technology module (850,000+ firms): digitisation widespread, cloud use common, but adoption of AI and other advanced technologies rare and concentrated in larger, older firms, so worker exposure exceeds firm-count adoption.
items.detail: Zolas, Kroff, Brynjolfsson, McElheran, Beede et al., 'Advanced Technologies Adoption and Use by Bloc A. Firms: Evidence from the Annual Business Survey', NBER Working Paper 28290, Dec 2020 (verified via web_extract this run; abstract only, no adoption percentage captured, so no value recorded). Different survey and question from BTOS; not splice-able.
